questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that I had already been in the city before and that I liked the city, as well that I knew people there

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy since I had already been on exchange there

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not get much information. Probably because I had already been on exchange there before

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed in a family members empty apartment. If you know anyone from the area it would be a good start to ask them if they know anyone renting out an apartment or a room

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: it might be harder to make friends and connections from school

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't think I had to do anything really. On my last exchange I had to do and index book which all serbian students have

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both from teachers and erasmus coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted as I knew this time around which classes would be available

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They are very calm about the whole process so do not stress about it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think it was a good level. Not too hard, not too easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: For one of the courses it was quite different as it was a discussion in the class the whole class about a movie about conflict we would watch every week. As for the other two it was mostly self studies which I haven't tried in UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Foreign policy of Serbia, History of Balkan relations, Peace and security through cinema

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Peace and security through cinema was really nice. it was fun to do a different kind of course were the main focus was movies. That is as well the class where the class was through discussions

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Taxis as the public transportation is not that good, especially after midnight

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are quite expensive for the standards in the country. I mean about same price as in Denmark. Dentist, hairdresser and things alike are really cheap compared to Denmark. At least 5 times cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not really hear of any. Only really with Erasmus welcome week

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend seeing some historic sites and learning more about the country and regions history

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend traveling around the country and the neighbouring countries. It is quite cheap to take the bus or train around and it is definitely worth going to see some other places in Serbia, Bosnia, Croatia, Montenegro, Kosovo

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy for me as I am Serbian myself and am really accustomed to the culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes it can be weird when it comes to the way Balkan people are not that aware of their social space and do not care to move in the supermarket if they are in the way or people will stop their cars in the middle of the street to talk to someone and let everyone else driving behind wait till they finish talking. Stuff like that is a little hard to get used to

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: What I really appreciate about Serbian people is the hospitality and how welcoming they are

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Learn some basics of the language beforehand, make sure you dont get scammed with the housing, perhaps consider where  you would like to go in the Balkans on holiday while you're in Belgrade

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect the unexpected. Belgrade is a big city where things always go wrong. You can never count on the public transportation and the streets of Belgrade will often have something unexpected going on, but that is one of the things I like about Belgrade

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining friendships. Both locals my own age and people from elsewhere from Erasmus. it is nice to gain insight to other cultures through friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say the language, as a good amount don't speak english even in the capital of Serbia and therefore it is basically necessary to know some Serbian.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
